arxiv-2108-03552.title: Prospects for measuring dark energy with 21 cm intensity mapping experiments
arxiv-2108-03552.creator: and Xin Zhang
arxiv-2108-03552.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by and Xin Zhang. Using the 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) technique can efficiently perform large-scale neutral hydrogen ( H i ) surveys, and this method has great potential for measuring dark-energy parameters. Some 21 cm IM experiments aiming at measuring dark energy in the redshift range of 0 < z < 3 0<z<3 have been proposed and performed, in which the typical ones using single-dish mode include e.g., BINGO, FAST, and SKA1-MID, and those using interferometric mode include e.g., HIRAX, CHIME, and Tianlai.

arxiv-2403-11449.title: Graph Partial Label Learning with Potential Cause Discovering
arxiv-2403-11449.creator: Hang Gao Jiaguo Yuan, Peng Qiao, Fengge Wu, Changwen Zheng, Huaping Liu
arxiv-2403-11449.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have garnered widespread attention for their potential to address the challenges posed by graph representation learning, which face complex graph-structured data across various domains. However, due to the inherent complexity and interconnectedness of graphs, accurately annotating graph data for training GNNs is extremely challenging.

arxiv-2407-03734.title: Improving Self-supervised Pre-training using Accent-Specific Codebooks
arxiv-2407-03734.description: Abstract Speech accents present a serious challenge to the performance of state-of-the-art end-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems. Even with self-supervised learning and pre-training of ASR models, accent invariance is seldom achieved. In this work, we propose an accent-aware adaptation technique for self-supervised learning that introduces a trainable set of accent-specific codebooks to the self-supervised architecture.

arxiv-2411-02686.title: On the d d -independence number in 1-planar graphs
arxiv-2411-02686.creator: Therese Biedl, Prosenjit Bose, Babak Miraftab
arxiv-2411-02686.description: Abstract Streszczenie The d d -independence number of a graph G G is the largest possible size of an independent set I I in G G where each vertex of I I has degree at least d d in G G .

arxiv-2502-00050.title: DISC : Dataset for Analyzing D riving Styles I n S imulated C rashes for Mixed Autonomy Thanks: The authors are with the Department of Computer Science, University of Maryland at College Park, MD, U.S.A. E-mail: {sandeept, sandip26, guruadp, sourang, lyzheng, lin}@umd.edu
arxiv-2502-00050.creator: Sandip Sharan Senthil Kumar, Sandeep Thalapanane
arxiv-2502-00050.description: Abstract Handling pre-crash scenarios is still a major challenge for self-driving cars due to limited practical data and human-driving behavior datasets. We introduce DISC (Driving Styles In Simulated Crashes), one of the first datasets designed to capture various driving styles and behaviors in pre-crash scenarios for mixed autonomy analysis.

arxiv-2503-20813.title: A Physics-Based Circuit Model for Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
arxiv-2503-20813.creator: Steven Louis \affilmark 1*, Hannah Bradley \affilmark 2, Artem Litvinenko \affilmark 3, Vasyl Tyberkevych \affilmark 2
arxiv-2503-20813.description: Abstract This work presents an equivalent circuit model for magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) that accurately reproduces their magnetization dynamics and electrical behavior within the macrospin approximation. The model is validated through direct numerical simulations of the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert–Slonczewski (LLGS) equation, encompassing ferromagnetic resonance, field- and spin-torque-induced switching, and spin-torque-induced oscillations.

pmc-10719245.title: Niacin restriction with NAMPT-inhibition is synthetic lethal to neuroendocrine carcinoma
pmc-10719245.creator: Miyuki Nomura, Mai Ohuchi, Yoshimi Sakamoto, Kei Kudo, Keisuke Yaku, Tomoyoshi Soga, Yuki Sugiura, Mami Morita, Kayoko Hayashi, Shuko Miyahara, Taku Sato, Yoji Yamashita, Shigemi Ito, Naohiko Kikuchi, Ikuro Sato, Rintaro Saito, Nobuo Yaegashi, Tatsuro Fukuhara, Hidekazu Yamada, Hiroshi Shima, Keiich
pmc-10719245.description: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) plays a major role in NAD biosynthesis in many cancers and is an attractive potential cancer target. However, factors dictating therapeutic efficacy of NAMPT inhibitors (NAMPTi) are unclear. We report that neuroendocrine phenotypes predict lung and prostate carcinoma vulnerability to NAMPTi, and that NAMPTi therapy against those cancers is enhanced by dietary modification.

pmc-11431702.title: Enhancing Functional Compounds in Sesame Oil through Acid-Soaking and Microwave-Heating of Sesame Seeds
pmc-11431702.creator: Jitkunya Yuenyong, Suchintana Limkoey, Chonlathit Phuksuk, Thitima Winan, Chonlada Bennett, Sudarat Jiamyangyuen, Sugunya Mahatheeranont, Phumon Sookwong

pmc-11492653.title: A case report on renal metastasis as an unusual presentation of choriocarcinoma
pmc-11492653.creator: Meimei Huang, Yu Ma
pmc-11492653.description: BackgroundChoriocarcinoma is an aggressively invasive neoplasm, characterized by its rapid proliferation and propensity for metastasis to distant organs via hematogenous dissemination. Lungs (80%), vagina (30%), pelvis (20%), liver (10%), and brain (10%) are the most frequently metastasized organs. Renal metastases are very rare. The clinical manifestations of choriocarcinoma varies depending on the site of disease, making diagnosis challenging.

pmc-12599058.title: Probiotics to reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia in adults with acute non‑anoxic brain injury: Study Protocol for a Double-Blind Multicenter Randomized International Clinical Trial (PROACT)
pmc-12599058.creator: Alberto Corriero, Rossana Soloperto, Mariateresa Giglio, Michele Salvagno, Paolo Trerotoli, Salvatore Grasso, Mario Ribezzi, Adriana Mosca, Claudio Petrillo, Nicolangelo De Toma, Giovanna Magnesa, Angelo Giacomucci, Riccardo Accattoli, Raffaella Maria Gadaleta, Marilina Florio, Marica Cariello, Anto
pmc-12599058.description: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a significant complication among critically ill patients, with associated mortality approaching 50%. Despite the implementation of established preventive strategies, additional interventions are urgently needed to further reduce the incidence of VAP. Probiotic therapy has emerged as a promising adjunctive approach; the benefits of probiotic therapy may be more pronounced in critically ill patients without pre-existing infections.

pmc-12631765.title: Epidemiology of Plasmodium spp. Detection Among Acute Febrile Illness Patients in Two Regions of Nigeria
pmc-12631765.creator: Claire A Quiner, Adamu Zigwai Ephraim, Vivian Kwaghe, Cyril Erameh, Jay Samuels, Lauren P Courtney, Jean H Kim, Osahogie Isaac Edeawe, Nankpah Vongdip, Onyia Justus Ejike, Ikponmwosa Odia, Kat Asman, Philippe Chebu, Jacqueline Agbukor, Oladimeji Damilare Matthew, Victoria Orok, Femi Owolagba, Blesse
pmc-12631765.description: BackgroundMalaria is a common cause of acute febrile illness (AFI) in Nigeria.MethodsPatients presenting with AFI at two tertiary hospitals were enrolled from August 2023 to September 2024. Specimens were screened for 25 pathogens using a multi-pathogen screening assay. Demographic, seasonal, clinical, and environmental associations with Plasmodium spp. detection via the assay are described and analyzed.

pmc-12721114.title: HHV-6–induced hydrocephalus with ventricular septa formation in an immunocompetent adult: illustrative case
pmc-12721114.creator: Umika Paul, Constance J. Mietus, Brittany Owusu-Adjei, Omar Sorour, Paramesh V. Karandikar, Mark D. Johnson
pmc-12721114.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) is a neurotropic virus known to induce encephalitis in immunocompromised patients as well as a subset of pediatric patients. However, ventriculitis secondary to HHV-6 is a rare occurrence among immunocompetent adults. Although acquired hydrocephalus has been described to infrequently co-occur with HHV-6 encephalitis in pediatric and immunocompromised adult patients, it has not been described in an immunocompetent adult.OBSERVATIONSThe authors present a rare case of HHV-6 encephalitis and obstructive hydrocephalus in an immunocompetent adult patient.

pmc-13238204.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of precision integrative nursing plans in nursing quality management at a digestive endoscopy center
pmc-13238204.creator: Na Zhao, Fengjuan Wang
pmc-13238204.description: Objective:To evaluate the effects of precision integrative nursing plans in nursing quality management at a digestive endoscopy centre.Methodology:This retrospective study involved three hundred patients diagnosed and treated at the digestive endoscopy centre of the Affiliated Hospital of Hebei University from January 2024 to June 2025.

pmc-13297504.title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction of Low BMD in Postmenopausal Women Using Cytokine, RANKL/OPG, and Oxidative Stress Biomarker Signatures: An Exploratory Study
pmc-13297504.creator: Fawaz Azizieh, Sedra M AlRamadan, Mahamed G. H. Omran
pmc-13297504.description: Aim: To evaluate cytokine, RANKL/OPG, and oxidative stress biomarker profiles in postmenopausal women with differing bone mineral density (BMD) and to apply machine learning (ML) models for early identification of low BMD. Materials & Methods: Seventy-one postmenopausal women were classified as normal BMD (N), osteopenia (OSN), or osteoporosis (OSR) using ISCD/WHO criteria.

pmc-13311448.title: Assessment of improvements in exercise tolerance following pulmonary valve replacement using physical accelerometry
pmc-13311448.creator: Nicholas Joy, Jonathan H. Soslow, Kimberly Crum, Mary Killian, Sudeep Sunthankar
pmc-13311448.description: Background:Pulmonary valve replacement may be required for patients with pulmonary valve disease. Exertional symptoms related to cardiovascular disease are an indication for pulmonary valve replacement; however, quantification of symptom improvement postoperatively is challenging, and previous studies have yielded mixed data. Accelerometry has the potential to remotely monitor changes in exercise tolerance following pulmonary valve replacement.

pmc-13486791.title: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of hepatic TMEM141 attenuates MASH and fibrosis via the ROS-HNF4α signaling pathway
pmc-13486791.creator: Jiayou Wang, Chwen-Lih Chen, Raja Gopoju, Shuwei Hu, Yang Wang, Hui Wang, Zaid Batayneh, Xiaoli Pan, Yeong-Renn Chen, Jeffrey Mellott, Patrick Kang, Lakshitha Gunawardana, Liya Yin, Yanqiao Zhang
pmc-13486791.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatoic liver disease (MASLD) and its advanced form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), have become a global epidemic due to obesity and genetic susceptibility. Here, we report transmembrane protein 141 (TMEM141), a protein with a largely unknown function, as a key regulator of MASH and MASH-associated fibrosis.

pmc-13546020.title: Nanoparticle-Based Drug Delivery Systems for Periodontitis: Antibacterial, Immunomodulatory, and Regenerative Strategies
pmc-13546020.creator: Liyan Wang, Yanwei Chen, Lu Li, Deshi Dong
pmc-13546020.description: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, and has become a serious public health issue. Antibacterial treatment and mechanical debridement are the main treatment strategies for periodontitis. However, side effects and bacterial resistance might lead to treatment failure. Nanotechnology systems have new opportunities for the management of periodontitis.

pmc-13668483.title: Postbiotics Unveiled: The Next Emerging Trend in Functional Foods
pmc-13668483.creator: Zoha Wahid, Abdul Momin Rizwan Ahmad, Farheen Zulfiqar, Syed Hassan Bin Usman Shah, Nilab Mohammadi
pmc-13668483.description: The global population is expected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, with demand for food increasing by up to 56%. Postbiotics are a safe and reliable substitute for probiotics, which are described as preparations of non‐viable bacteria and/or their metabolic byproducts. Data for this narrative review was collected using Goggle scholar and PubMed from 2006 to 2026.

pmc-13684597.title: Parabrachial-amygdala circuit cooperates with a posterior striatal area to drive opioid withdrawal aversion
pmc-13684597.creator: Seung-Chan Lee, Kelsey Shimoda, Jesse Ross, Jensine Coudriet, Thomas Jhou, Satoshi Ikemoto
pmc-13684597.description: Opioid addiction treatment is often hampered by the severe dysphoria of opioid withdrawal, but withdrawal treatments are limited by incomplete understanding of brain mechanisms involved. One area frequently implicated in withdrawal symptoms is the central amygdala, whose capsular portion (CeC) is particularly strongly activated during withdrawal.
